mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 0.05% over the prior 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as market participants anticipate lower financing costs for corporate expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.05% for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is consistently below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.5% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending capacity and corporate revenue growth, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 6.5% for 2 consecutive months, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) below their 3-month moving averages indicates weakening consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate reduced corporate revenue growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline below 3-month moving average
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL rising above 2.5% annualized), the Federal Reserve is likely to implement aggressive monetary tightening, causing a sell-off in equities and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% annualized, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth (GDPC1) above 3.0% annualized over the prior quarter signals strong economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings growth and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 60% of instances when GDPC1 > 3.0% annualized, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is consistently below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95% of its 12-month moving average, it indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output capacity and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95% of 12-month moving average, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.0% indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending power and corporate hiring, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS decline and UNRATE > 6.0% does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of manufacturing expansion (INDPRO rising above 100% of its 12-month moving average), robust production capacity supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO > 100% of 12-month moving average, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
